newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast floats stake in oilseed firm Trituraf.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast floats stake in oilseed firm Trituraf.

text.p: A 10 percent stake in oilseed producer Trituraf owned by the Ivory Coast government is to be sold to the public, Ivory Coast's Privatisation Committee said in a sale prospectus.
It said 104,000 shares, representing the state's 10 percent stake, would be offered to the public between June 2 and 30 (eds: correct June 2 - 30) at a price of 6,250 CFA francs ($10.8) per share.
Trituraf is majority-owned by Anglo-Dutch food and household products group Unilever, which will retain its 73 percent stake.
France's Compagnie Francaise de Developpement des Textiles (CFDT) will also retain its 14 percent stake. The balance of three percent is currently owned by private Ivorian interests.

Trituraf, which employs 342 people, had turnover of 21.34 billion CFA francs in 1995/96, when it showed an operating profit of 843.2 million CFA francs and a net profit of 561.3 million, according to the prospectus.

For 1996/97, the prospectus is forecasting turnover of 22.09 billion CFA francs, rising to 25.71 billion by 2000/01. Net profit, again according to the prospectus, is forecast to rise to 596 million CFA francs in 1996/97, rising to 770 million by 2000/01.
The exact end of each financial year was not immediately available. ($ = 580 CFA francs)
